---
title: "Install MISP 3.0 on Rocky Linux"
---

This guide installs the [MISP `3.0_wip` branch](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/tree/3.0_wip) on a clean Rocky Linux 9 or 10 server.
It uses Apache with PHP-FPM, MariaDB, Redis or Valkey, and Supervisor.
The checkout lives in `/var/www/MISP` and runs as the distribution's `apache` account.

::: {.callout-note}
`3.0_wip` is the MISP 3.0 development branch.
Evaluate it on an isolated server before deployment.
For an existing MISP 2.5 database, follow the [offline upgrade guide](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd).
:::

The package and application checks used Rocky Linux 9.9 and 10.3 x86_64 containers with services started directly.
They used MISP [`3.0_wip` commit `cd8a4f41`](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/commit/cd8a4f416438174389d57307894039ce0c75f6c9).
Verify systemd startup, firewall rules, and SELinux enforcement on the target host.

## Prepare the host and install packages {#rocky-install-packages}

Use a current Rocky Linux 9 or 10 minor release, a `sudo` account, a DNS name, and a trusted TLS certificate and key for that name.
Keep web access restricted to administrators until you change the bootstrap password.

Enable CRB and EPEL for your Rocky Linux release.
EPEL supplies Supervisor and the fuzzy-hash development library.
These commands use Rocky Linux's BaseOS, AppStream, CRB, and Extras repositories. [Rocky Linux repositories](https://docs.rockylinux.org/guides/package_management/dnf_package_manager/) · [Fedora EPEL setup](https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/epel/getting-started/)

```bash
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh
sudo dnf install dnf-plugins-core
sudo dnf config-manager --set-enabled crb
sudo dnf install epel-release
sudo dnf repolist
```

::: {.table-responsive}

| Component | Rocky Linux 9 | Rocky Linux 10 |
|---|---|---|
| PHP | Enable the AppStream `php:8.3` stream | Install the distribution's PHP packages |
| MariaDB | Enable the AppStream `mariadb:10.11` stream | Install `mariadb-server` |
| Cache and queues | `redis` package and service | `valkey` package and service |

:::

MISP requires MariaDB 10.11 or later for this procedure.
On Rocky Linux 10, MISP connects to Valkey through the PHP Redis extension and uses the same Redis settings. [MISP software requirements](../requirements/index.qmd#software-requirements)

On **Rocky Linux 9**, select the streams before installing PHP or MariaDB.

```bash
sudo dnf module enable php:8.3 mariadb:10.11
sudo dnf install mariadb-server redis
```

On **Rocky Linux 10**, install MariaDB and Valkey.

```bash
sudo dnf install mariadb-server valkey
```

On **both releases**, install the common dependencies and check PHP's database and cache extensions.
The `/usr/bin/curl` dependency also accepts `curl-minimal` on minimal installations.

```bash
sudo dnf install git /usr/bin/curl ca-certificates openssl unzip file-libs gnupg2 procps-ng iproute \
  httpd mod_ssl php-cli php-fpm php-mysqlnd php-mbstring php-xml \
  php-gd php-intl php-bcmath php-pecl-zip php-pecl-redis6 \
  python3.12 python3.12-pip python3.12-devel gcc ssdeep-devel \
  policycoreutils-python-utils supervisor
php --version
php --ri pdo_mysql
php --ri redis
mariadb --version
```

Set a shared PHP memory limit before running the initialization commands.
Both the CLI and PHP-FPM load `/etc/php.d/99-misp.ini`.
A 2 GiB limit gives the initial definitions import and larger MISP jobs room to run. [MISP RPM installation](https://github.com/MISP/MISP-RPM/blob/master/INSTALL.md)

```bash
sudo tee /etc/php.d/99-misp.ini > /dev/null <<'INI'
memory_limit = 2048M
INI
php -r 'echo ini_get("memory_limit"), PHP_EOL;'
sudo php-fpm -i | grep '^memory_limit '
```

Both checks should show `2048M`.
If the `apache` PHP-FPM pool sets `memory_limit` separately, match the limit in the pool configuration as well.
Inspect the pool with `sudo php-fpm -tt`.

## Check out MISP and install its dependencies {#rocky-install-source}

Install Composer at `/usr/local/bin/composer` using the checksum-verified installer procedure.
Run Git, Composer, and the Python environment as `apache`. [Composer installation and verification](https://getcomposer.org/download/)

```bash
sudo install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0755 /var/www/MISP
sudo install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0750 /var/lib/misp \
  /var/lib/misp/composer /var/lib/misp/attachments
sudo -u apache git clone --branch 3.0_wip --depth 1 \
  --recurse-submodules --shallow-submodules \
  https://github.com/MISP/MISP.git /var/www/MISP
sudo -u apache git -C /var/www/MISP rev-parse HEAD

sudo -u apache env COMPOSER_HOME=/var/lib/misp/composer \
  /usr/local/bin/composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app \
  install --no-dev --no-interaction --prefer-dist
sudo -u apache env COMPOSER_HOME=/var/lib/misp/composer \
  /usr/local/bin/composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app \
  check-platform-reqs --no-dev
sudo -u apache python3.12 -m venv /var/www/MISP/venv
sudo -u apache env HOME=/var/lib/misp /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python \
  -m pip install -r /var/www/MISP/requirements.txt
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip check
```

## Initialize MariaDB and MISP {#rocky-install-database}

Create `/etc/my.cnf.d/90-misp.cnf`, owned by root with mode `0644`, to bind MariaDB to loopback.

```ini
[mariadb]
bind-address=127.0.0.1
```

Keep the cache listener on loopback and protected mode enabled.
Use `systemctl cat redis.service` on Rocky Linux 9 or `systemctl cat valkey.service` on Rocky Linux 10 to locate the packaged configuration file.
Start MariaDB and the cache service for your release.

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now mariadb
```

```bash
# Rocky Linux 9
sudo systemctl enable --now redis
redis-cli ping
```

```bash
# Rocky Linux 10
sudo systemctl enable --now valkey
valkey-cli ping
```

After the cache returns `PONG`, open a MariaDB administrator session over the local socket with history disabled.

```bash
sudo env MYSQL_HISTFILE=/dev/null mariadb --protocol=socket
```

Create the database and a user for the application's loopback TCP connection.
Replace the placeholder with a unique database password.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE misp
    CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci;
CREATE USER 'misp'@'127.0.0.1' IDENTIFIED BY 'REPLACE_WITH_DATABASE_PASSWORD';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON misp.* TO 'misp'@'127.0.0.1';
EXIT;
```

Import the schema and copy the application configuration templates from the same checkout.

```bash
sudo mariadb --protocol=socket misp < /var/www/MISP/INSTALL/MARIADB.sql
for name in bootstrap core database config; do
  sudo install -o apache -g apache -m 0640 \
    "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.default.php" "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.php"
done
```

In `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/database.php`, set `host` to `127.0.0.1`, `login` to `misp`, and `password` to the database password.
Keep `database` set to `misp`.

Update the corresponding keys under `MISP` in `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/config.php`, using your DNS name and organization.

```php
'baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'external_baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'org' => 'Your organization',
'osuser' => 'apache',
'python_bin' => '/var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python',
'attachments_dir' => '/var/lib/misp/attachments',
'redis_host' => '127.0.0.1',
'background_jobs' => false,
```

Generate an instance salt with `openssl rand -hex 32` and set `Security.salt` in the same file.
Run the initialization commands as `apache` and store the bootstrap API key in a root-only file.

```bash
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin runUpdates
sudo sh -c 'umask 077
runuser -u apache -- /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake User init \
  > /root/misp-bootstrap-api-key'
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics
```

Confirm that schema diagnostics report zero pending and failed migrations.

### Set up the instance signing key {#rocky-install-gnupg}

Generate an OpenPGP signing key as `apache` for protected synchronization and signed notifications.
Use a private Bash session and replace `misp@example.org` with the instance's signing address.

```bash
sudo install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0700 /var/lib/misp/gnupg
gpg_email=misp@example.org
read -r -s -p 'Instance GnuPG passphrase: ' gpg_passphrase
printf '\n'
printf '%s\n' "$gpg_passphrase" | sudo -u apache /usr/bin/gpg \
  --homedir /var/lib/misp/gnupg --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-fd 0 \
  --quick-generate-key "$gpg_email" ed25519 sign never
unset gpg_passphrase
sudo -u apache /usr/bin/gpg --homedir /var/lib/misp/gnupg --armor \
  --output /var/www/MISP/app/webroot/gpg.asc --export "$gpg_email"
sudo -u apache /usr/bin/gpgconf --homedir /var/lib/misp/gnupg --kill gpg-agent
```

Stopping the agent from the setup session lets PHP-FPM start it in the web service's SELinux context.
In `app/Config/config.php`, set `GnuPG.homedir` to `/var/lib/misp/gnupg`, `GnuPG.email` to the signing address, and `GnuPG.password` to the passphrase.
Keep `GnuPG.binary` set to `/usr/bin/gpg` and leave `GnuPG.sign` enabled for signed email.
MISP encrypts outgoing OpenPGP email using recipients' public keys.
Include the instance's private key and configuration in protected backups. [Instance and user keys](../cryptographic-keys/index.qmd)

## Serve HTTPS with SELinux enforcing {#rocky-install-web}

Apply persistent SELinux labels to the paths the web process writes to.
The application source under `/var/www` uses the distribution's web content policy.

```bash
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/www/MISP/app/(Config|tmp|files/scripts/tmp)(/.*)?'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_content_t '/var/lib/misp'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/lib/misp/attachments(/.*)?'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_var_run_t '/var/lib/misp/gnupg(/.*)?'
sudo restorecon -F /var/lib/misp
sudo restorecon -RF /var/www/MISP /var/lib/misp/attachments /var/lib/misp/gnupg
sudo setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect_db on
sudo setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect on
```

With the stock Rocky Linux targeted policy and its default `httpd_use_gpg` setting, GnuPG and its agent run in the PHP-FPM SELinux domain.
The `httpd_var_run_t` label allows that domain to create the agent's Unix sockets in the GnuPG home.
The database boolean permits the web process to connect to MariaDB.
The network boolean permits other outbound connections from the web process, including Redis or Valkey and Supervisor.
Apply your site's network policy to the services MISP should reach. [SELinux administration](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html/using_selinux/index)

Use the distribution's Apache PHP-FPM integration and the `apache` pool.
In `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf`, replace the example TLS virtual host and keep the global TLS settings, including `Listen 443 https`.
Use your hostname and the paths to its certificate chain and private key.

```apache
<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    DocumentRoot /var/www/MISP/app/webroot
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/misp-fullchain.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/pki/tls/private/misp.key

    <Directory /var/www/MISP/app/webroot>
        Options -Indexes
        AllowOverride FileInfo
        Require all granted
        DirectoryIndex index.php
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
```

The checkout's `app/webroot/.htaccess` provides the rewrite and API authorization rules.
Check that the default FPM pool listens on `/run/php-fpm/www.sock` and allows access by `apache`.

```bash
sudo restorecon -v /etc/pki/tls/certs/misp-fullchain.pem /etc/pki/tls/private/misp.key
sudo php-fpm -t
sudo httpd -t
sudo systemctl enable --now php-fpm httpd
```

If you use firewalld, check the active zones with `sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones` and allow the HTTPS service in the zone used for administration.
Sign in over HTTPS as `admin@admin.test` with the bootstrap password `admin`.
Change the password on first login before granting other clients access.

## Start the background workers {#rocky-install-workers}

Configure Supervisor's authenticated loopback API in `/etc/supervisord.conf`.
Add or update the following section with a dedicated password, for example one generated with `openssl rand -hex 24`.

```ini
[inet_http_server]
port=127.0.0.1:9001
username=supervisor
password=REPLACE_WITH_SUPERVISOR_PASSWORD
```

Create one worker for each queue and a separate scheduler.

```bash
{
  printf '%s\n' '[group:misp-workers]' \
    'programs=default,email,cache,prio,update,scheduler'
  for worker in default email cache prio update scheduler; do
    if [ "$worker" = scheduler ]; then
      cake_command=scheduler_worker
    else
      cake_command="start_worker $worker"
    fi
    cat <<EOF

[program:$worker]
command=/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake $cake_command
directory=/var/www/MISP
user=apache
autostart=true
autorestart=true
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/www/MISP/app/tmp/logs/$worker-worker.log
EOF
  done
} | sudo tee /etc/supervisord.d/misp-workers.ini > /dev/null
```

In `app/Config/config.php`, set `SimpleBackgroundJobs.redis_host` and `SimpleBackgroundJobs.supervisor_host` to `127.0.0.1`.
Set `supervisor_user` and `supervisor_password` in that section to match Supervisor and keep its port at `9001`.
Set `MISP.background_jobs` to `true`.

```bash
sudo chmod 0600 /etc/supervisord.conf
sudo systemctl enable --now supervisord
sudo systemctl reload php-fpm
sudo supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
```

Once all six processes report `RUNNING`, check worker status and wait for a test job to complete in MISP. [Background worker checks](../administration/index.qmd#admin-background-jobs)

## Verify the installation {#rocky-install-verify}

- Run `ss -lnt` to confirm that MariaDB, Redis or Valkey, and Supervisor are bound to loopback.
- Check the HTTPS certificate and sign-in from a client that trusts your CA, then create and find a synthetic event with **Your organisation only** distribution.
- Check that **GnuPG** reports **OK** under **Administration → Server Settings & Maintenance → Services** with SELinux enforcing before using protected synchronization or signed mail. [System health checks](../administration/index.qmd#server-settings-and-maintenance)
- Verify a completed background job, then review the site organization, distribution defaults, mail settings, and backup and restore procedures before enabling sync or scheduled feeds. [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login)

For a 2.5 upgrade on Rocky Linux, run the migration's Cake commands as `apache` and restart `php-fpm` after the migration.
